paper_metadata.title: Extrapolation method to optimize linear-ramp QAOA parameters: Evaluation of QAOA runtime scaling

experiments.description: Linear-ramp QAOA with extrapolated parameters evaluated on portfolio optimization instances of increasing size (N=12 to 28), using noiseless simulation and comparing runtime scaling against classical heuristics.

algorithm.variant: linear-ramp QAOA (LR-QAOA) with extrapolated parameter setting
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA with transverse-field mixer and cost Hamiltonian
algorithm.num_layers: p optimized per instance; reported examples include p = 128, 215, 304, 608; initial p0 = 6 for smallest subproblem
algorithm.convergence_criteria: local minimum of estimated total depth D on a logarithmically spaced p-grid

hyperparameters.budget_constraint_B: N/2 for even N, (N-1)/2 for odd N
hyperparameters.penalty_prefactor_A: computed using routine from Ref. [22], then kept constant during extrapolation
hyperparameters.shots_formula: median shots from Nshots = log(1/2) / log(1 - Popt)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Extrapolated from optimized parameters on smaller subproblems (N=4,6,8,10); initial p0=6 for first grid search

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 binary variable per asset; portfolio weights z_i ∈ {0,1}; budget constraint encoded via quadratic penalty
problem_formulation.objective_function: F_portfolio(z) = q * sum_{i,j} z_i z_j sigma_ij - (1-q) * sum_i z_i mu_i + A (sum_i z_i - B)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: budget constraint enforced by quadratic penalty term with prefactor A
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: cost Hamiltonian defined by F(z) with basis-state encoding F̂|z⟩ = F(z)|z⟩

problem_instance.description: Randomly sampled subsets of DAX 30 assets; instances generated for sizes N = 12 to 28, with smaller subinstances of sizes 4, 6, 8, 10 used for parameter extrapolation

dataset_specification.preprocessing: annualized returns and covariance matrices; random selection of N assets from 30; budget set to half the assets

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Annualized returns and covariance matrices computed from historical DAX 30 data; random asset subsampling; budget B adjusted with N
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 random problem instances per N; extrapolation based on 10 random subinstances per subproblem size; noiseless quantum simulation; runtime measured as total depth D

quantum_resources.num_qubits: N (up to 28 in main experiments; subproblems use 4, 6, 8, 10)
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: QAOA depth p; total depth D = d * Nshots; single-circuit depth d roughly proportional to p

implementation_details.classical_solver: MQLib/Burer2002 used as classical baseline for comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: random sub-instance sampling; grid search over log(delta_gamma), log(delta_beta); skew-Gaussian fit; extrapolation to larger N; p optimization by local search on logarithmic grid
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute median shots from success probability; total depth D = d * Nshots; exponential fit of D vs N

speedup_claims.conditions: portfolio optimization, noiseless simulation, N=12 to 28, LR-QAOA with extrapolated parameters
speedup_claims.caveats: Only an indication of quantum scaling advantage; not a proven asymptotic speedup. Parameter-finding cost is not included in the runtime comparison.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial scaling suggested if Popt remains constant and p ∝ N^3
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming the conjectured constant success probability extends to larger N
speedup_claims.caveats: Authors explicitly state that larger problem sizes beyond N=28 are needed to resolve exponential vs polynomial scaling.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Empirically fitted runtime scaling D ∝ 2^(0.22 N) for portfolio optimization; discussion suggests possible polynomial scaling if Popt remains constant and p ∝ N^3
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Empirically fitted baseline scaling for MQLib/Burer2002: T ∝ 2^(0.328 N)

experiments.description: Linear-ramp QAOA with extrapolated parameters evaluated on feature selection instances derived from the German Credit Data, with scaling compared against classical heuristics.

algorithm.variant: linear-ramp QAOA (LR-QAOA) with extrapolated parameter setting
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA with transverse-field mixer and cost Hamiltonian
algorithm.num_layers: p optimized per instance; scaling shown for N = 12 to 28
algorithm.convergence_criteria: local minimum of estimated total depth D on a logarithmically spaced p-grid

hyperparameters.shots_formula: median shots from Nshots = log(1/2) / log(1 - Popt)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Extrapolated from optimized parameters on smaller subproblems (N=4,6,8,10); initial p0=6 for first grid search

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 binary variable per feature after one-hot encoding; z_i = 1 means feature selected
problem_formulation.objective_function: F_feature(z) = - (phi * sum_i z_i |rho_{i,Y}| - (1-phi) * sum_{i != j} z_i z_j |rho_{i,j}| )
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: no explicit hard constraint; feature selection tradeoff encoded directly in objective
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: cost Hamiltonian defined by F(z) with basis-state encoding F̂|z⟩ = F(z)|z⟩

problem_instance.description: Feature selection on the German Credit Data after one-hot encoding; instances generated by selecting subsets of features

dataset_specification.preprocessing: one-hot encoding of categorical features; linear correlation used as dependence measure

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: 7 numerical and 13 categorical attributes; one-hot encoding expands to max 48 binary features; correlations computed between features and target
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 random problem instances per N; extrapolation based on 10 random subinstances per subproblem size; noiseless quantum simulation; runtime measured as total depth D

quantum_resources.num_qubits: N (up to 48 binary variables; experiments shown for N = 12 to 28 in scaling plots)
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: QAOA depth p; total depth D = d * Nshots; single-circuit depth d roughly proportional to p

implementation_details.classical_solver: MQLib/Burer2002 used as classical baseline for comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: random sub-instance sampling; grid search over log(delta_gamma), log(delta_beta); skew-Gaussian fit; extrapolation to larger N; p optimization by local search on logarithmic grid
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute median shots from success probability; total depth D = d * Nshots; exponential fit of D vs N

speedup_claims.factor: worse scaling than classical baseline (0.46 vs 0.2)
speedup_claims.conditions: feature selection on German Credit Data, noiseless simulation, N=12 to 28
speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum advantage observed; some outliers with very large D indicate instability of extrapolation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Empirically fitted runtime scaling D ∝ 2^(0.46 N) for feature selection
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Empirically fitted baseline scaling for MQLib/Burer2002: T ∝ 2^(0.2 N)

experiments.description: Linear-ramp QAOA with extrapolated parameters evaluated on clustering instances from the Moons dataset, with scaling compared against classical heuristics.

algorithm.variant: linear-ramp QAOA (LR-QAOA) with extrapolated parameter setting
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA with transverse-field mixer and cost Hamiltonian
algorithm.num_layers: p optimized per instance; scaling shown for N = 12 to 28
algorithm.convergence_criteria: local minimum of estimated total depth D on a logarithmically spaced p-grid

hyperparameters.shots_formula: median shots from Nshots = log(1/2) / log(1 - Popt)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Extrapolated from optimized parameters on smaller subproblems (N=4,6,8,10); initial p0=6 for first grid search

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 binary variable per data point; clustering reduced to Max-Cut on a fully connected graph with edge weights given by pairwise Euclidean distances
problem_formulation.objective_function: F_clustering(z) = sum_{i,j} w_ij (z_i + z_j - 2 z_i z_j)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: binary partition into two clusters; no explicit penalty term
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: cost Hamiltonian defined by F(z) with basis-state encoding F̂|z⟩ = F(z)|z⟩

problem_instance.description: Binary clustering / Max-Cut instances built from the Moons dataset; each data point corresponds to one binary decision variable

dataset_specification.preprocessing: pairwise Euclidean distances used to build dense graph adjacency matrix

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Two-dimensional synthetic dataset; distances converted to weighted graph for Max-Cut formulation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 random problem instances per N; extrapolation based on 10 random subinstances per subproblem size; noiseless quantum simulation; runtime measured as total depth D

quantum_resources.num_qubits: N (number of data points / binary variables; scaling shown for N = 12 to 28)
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: QAOA depth p; total depth D = d * Nshots; single-circuit depth d roughly proportional to p

implementation_details.classical_solver: MQLib/Burer2002 used as classical baseline for comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: random sub-instance sampling; grid search over log(delta_gamma), log(delta_beta); skew-Gaussian fit; extrapolation to larger N; p optimization by local search on logarithmic grid
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute median shots from success probability; total depth D = d * Nshots; exponential fit of D vs N

speedup_claims.conditions: clustering on Moons dataset, noiseless simulation, N=12 to 28
speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum advantage observed; a few outliers at larger N.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Empirically fitted runtime scaling D ∝ 2^(0.25 N) for clustering (Moons)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Empirically fitted baseline scaling for MQLib/Burer2002: T ∝ 2^(0.061 N)

experiments.description: Classical baseline runtime evaluation for portfolio optimization, feature selection, and clustering using CPLEX, Gurobi, MQLib/Burer2002, and Goemans-Williamson; included because it is used as the comparison baseline for the quantum experiments.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: same QUBO instances as quantum experiments
problem_formulation.objective_function: portfolio / feature selection / clustering QUBO objectives

problem_instance.description: Same portfolio, feature selection, and clustering instances used for quantum comparison
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: runtime measured five times per instance across ten instances per N; scaling fit T ∝ 2^(alpha N)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: ten random instances per N; five runtime repetitions per instance
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: robust log2-linear fit of runtime scaling

speedup_claims.conditions: runtime benchmarking for portfolio optimization, feature selection, clustering (Moons and Blobs)
speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment provides classical benchmark scaling only; no quantum result is reported here.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Empirical exponential fits reported: portfolio CPLEX 2^(0.09 N), Gurobi 2^(0.777 N), MQLib/Burer2002 2^(0.328 N), GW 2^(0.171 N); feature selection CPLEX 2^(0.056 N), Gurobi 2^(0.171 N), MQLib/Burer2002 2^(0.2 N), GW 2^(0.135 N); clustering (Moons) CPLEX 2^(0.063 N), Gurobi 2^(0.034 N), MQLib/Burer2002 2^(0.061 N), GW 2^(0.107 N); clustering (Blobs) CPLEX 2^(0.028 N), Gurobi 2^(0.044 N), MQLib/Burer2002 2^(0.054 N), GW 2^(0.079 N)
